parsedVerdict.reasoning:
src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts does the work an application-layer use case is supposed to do. It checks the incoming status string, loads the order and its products through a lookup service, and leaves the state transition to the domain (order.advanceTo). It leaves the stock arithmetic to a domain service (StockAllocationService.dispatch), saves through domain repository interfaces, and maps the result to a DTO.

The file holds no persistence code, transport code or framework code. It also holds no business calculations of its own.

The one borderline spot is the check `if (order.status === 'shipped')`. It decides when stock is dispatched. This is coordination between two aggregates (the order and the products), not a business calculation, and the rule itself is carried out by the domain service. Coordinating effects across aggregates after a state change is a normal job for a use case.
